topic: Twenty-six practical Claude habits that beginner walkthroughs leave out, in six groups: set it up once (Instructions, memory, memory off for one chat), ask so the first answer lands (one full message, briefing like a new colleague, saying what and why, one example, long documents first, search vs Research), projects, files and artifacts (projects, short instructions and decision notes, what Claude reads in files, asking for the finished file, skills), checking the work (permission to say I don't know, tracing claims, the Thinking section, checking 'sent'), making usage last (effort and model, fresh chats with a handover, connectors, Settings > Usage) and handing bigger jobs to Cowork (outcome and one folder, approval modes, scheduled tasks, computer use)
audience: People who already use Claude for work and get decent answers, but lose time to long chats, repeated explanations, unchecked numbers and usage limits
goal: Pick up five habits first (Instructions, one full message, tracing every claim, handing over to a fresh chat, checking Settings > Usage), then add the rest one at a time
notes: Claude saves memory as a set of individual topics as you chat, rather than summarising conversations after they end. Mention that a deadline moved, and your next conversation already knows. You can also tell Claude to 'remember this'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra plans on the web, Claude Desktop and Claude Mobile. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners control whether memory is available. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

See what Claude remembers in Settings > Your Claude by selecting 'Manage' next to Your memory (Settings > Memory in the older Settings layout). Everything Claude remembers is listed under Topics. Select a topic to read it, then use the edit icon to change it or select 'Delete' to remove it. Fix something in one topic and the change applies to every conversation from then on. You can also tell Claude in a chat what to remember, change or forget, and the update applies to your next conversation. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Settings > Your Claude also has the 'Generate memory from chats' setting (memory on or off for your account) and the 'Search and reference chats' toggle. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Instructions: click your initials in the lower left corner, select Settings, then Your Claude ('Account' in the older Settings layout). Under 'Instructions', describe your preferred approaches or methods, common terms or concepts you use, typical scenarios you encounter and general communication instructions. Anything you add there applies to all of your conversations. Project instructions apply only to chats within that project. Use skills when you want to customise how Claude formats and delivers its responses. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically for specialised tasks; they are available on all plans and require code execution to be on. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills]

Settings also has a Capabilities page: artifacts need the code execution and file creation setting ('Create and edit files' in the updated layout) turned on in Settings > Capabilities. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them] Code execution and file creation is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude]

Turn memory off for a single chat (web, Claude Desktop and the latest Claude Mobile): start a new chat, click '+' in the message box, click 'Memory' to turn it off, then send your first message. It must be turned off before the first message; once the chat starts, the setting can't be changed. After the first message, a crossed-out memory icon appears next to the chat title. Claude won't use what it remembers in that chat and saves nothing from it to memory. Unlike an incognito chat, the chat stays in your chat history and Claude can still find it when searching past chats from your other conversations. It works the same way in projects. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Incognito chats: when you start a new chat outside a project, click the ghost icon in the upper right corner. Incognito chats aren't saved to your chat history or to Claude's memory, aren't used for training, and are retained for 30 days by default (or longer under an Enterprise organisation's custom retention). Claude won't pull information from incognito chats when searching previous conversations. They are available on all plans. With the new Claude experience, Claude can't create files or run code in incognito chats. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12260368-use-incognito-chats]

Anthropic's usage-limit best practices: plan your conversation before you start (what you need, whether you can combine related questions into one message, what background you can give upfront); be specific and concise and include relevant context, avoiding vague queries that need clarification; batch related tasks or questions in one message; review and edit your prompt before sending to reduce follow-up messages; refer back to earlier information instead of repeating it; for writing, send the entire text for editing in one message rather than breaking it up; for research and analysis, provide all relevant data in a single, well-structured message. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Searching past chats is available on paid plans (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise) on the web, Claude Desktop and Claude Mobile. Ask naturally, for example 'What did we discuss about [topic]?', 'Can you find our conversation about [subject]?' or 'Let's continue where we left off with [project].' The search shows in the chat as a tool call. Inside a project, searches are limited to that project's chats. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Web search: if you have the new Claude experience, there's no web search toggle and Claude searches the web when it helps; otherwise turn it on with '+' > 'Web search'. Every response that uses web search includes citations, so you can verify the sources yourself. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10684626-enable-and-use-web-search]

Web search is best for straightforward, factual queries that can be answered with one or two tool calls. Research is best for comprehensive information gathering requiring five or more tool calls over 1-3 minutes, and produces a longer report with citations. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11095361-when-should-i-use-web-search-extended-thinking-and-research]
Research is on paid plans, needs web search on, and is turned on with '+' > 'Research'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-use-research-on-claude]

To make the most of your context window and usage limits: turn off apps you've connected when a conversation doesn't need them, and ask Claude not to search the web when you don't need current information. Tools and connectors are token-intensive. Choose a lower effort level for routine tasks; higher effort uses more tokens. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Connectors in a conversation: click the '+' button in the lower left of the chat (or type '/'), hover over 'Connectors' and toggle on the specific services you want Claude to use for that conversation. Under Connectors, 'Tool access' sets how connectors load: Auto is the default and works well for most people; with 10 or more connectors active, Anthropic suggests switching to On demand to give conversations more room. Connected services are managed in Customize > Connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities]

Claude can hallucinate incorrect or misleading information. It can display quotes that look authoritative or sound convincing but are not grounded in fact. Users should not rely on Claude as a singular source of truth and should carefully scrutinise any high-stakes advice. With web search results, review Claude's cited sources: original websites may contain important context or details not included in Claude's synthesis. The thumbs down button lets you flag an unhelpful response. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on]

Claude can hallucinate its own capabilities: it can produce links that don't work and falsely claim it has sent emails or produced external documents. Even if it claims otherwise, Claude has no access to tools or software that aren't explicitly integrated, including email, word processors or file transfers. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241188-claude-is-producing-links-that-don-t-work-and-falsely-claiming-that-it-has-sent-emails-or-produced-external-documents-what-s-going-on]

Thinking can't be turned off in Claude on Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 or Opus 5. When thinking is on, you see a 'Thinking' indicator and an expandable 'Thinking' section above Claude's response; click it to view a summary of Claude's thought process, which can be valuable for verifying how Claude arrived at its conclusion. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Models may not know about events after their training cutoff. Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 are trained on data up to June 2026. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114494-how-up-to-date-is-claude-s-training-data]

Claude analyses images and charts only in PDFs of 100 pages or fewer; for PDFs of 101 to 1000 pages it processes text only, and for non-PDF documents it extracts text only. Supported uploads include PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX documents and JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images, up to 500MB per file and 20 files per chat. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-upload-files-to-claude]
Claude doesn't generate photos or illustrations, but it can analyse images you upload. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9002504-can-claude-produce-images]

Projects are self-contained workspaces with their own chat histories and knowledge bases. They are available to all users; Free users can create up to five. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects]

Create a project: hover over the left side and click 'Projects' (or go to claude.ai/projects), click '+ New Project' in the upper right corner, and give it a name and description; Claude will not have access to the name and description. Add files with the '+' button in the project knowledge, on the right side of the project's page; anything there is used across all chats in that project. Click 'Set project instructions', add instructions, then click 'Save instructions'. Context is not shared across chats within a project unless it is added to the project knowledge base. Move a standalone chat into a project with the dropdown arrow next to the chat name, then 'Add to project'. Star a project with the star icon in its upper right corner. Each project has its own memory; turn off 'Use account memory' under Memory on the project's page to keep it fully separate. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects]

Project caching: content in projects is cached and counts less against your limits when reused. Upload your core working documents to project knowledge when you start a project. Caches expire after a period of inactivity: if you come back after a long break, your first message counts that content in full again. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Keep project instructions short: use them for general context about the project, key guidelines and Claude's role, and keep task-specific instructions for the chat itself. Regularly remove project files you're no longer using. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

The model menu next to the send button controls the model, the effort level and thinking. To change effort: click the model name next to the send button, click 'Effort', and choose a level; each model's recommended level is marked 'Default'. Low and Medium work well for routine tasks and stretch your usage further; High offers the best overall balance of quality and speed; Extra high (Opus 4.7 and newer) is for long-running coding and agentic tasks; Max is the most thorough, for the deepest reasoning, with longer response times. Higher effort takes longer and uses more tokens, so you reach your usage limits faster. You can change the model, effort or thinking at any point in a conversation; changes apply from Claude's next response. For everyday tasks the defaults work well. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Usage limits: most accounts have a limit that resets on a rolling five-hour session window, and paid plans add weekly limits; there's no fixed message count. [https://claude.com/pricing] The five-hour period starts when you send your first message and resets in full five hours later. Weekly limits reset at a fixed day and time assigned to your account. You can see what you've used, and the time remaining, under Current session in Settings > Usage, and your next weekly reset there too. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

On Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans, Settings > Usage shows progress bars for your five-hour session and weekly limits: Current session (how much you've used and the time remaining) and Weekly limits (when they reset). [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

What uses your limits faster: message length, file attachment size, current conversation length, tool use (such as Research and web search), model choice, effort level, artifact creation and use, and multi-step tasks such as running code, creating files or browsing websites. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Long chats: with code execution on, when a conversation approaches the context window limit, Claude summarises earlier messages to continue; you may see Claude 'organizing its thoughts'. Longer conversations that trigger this automatic context management consume more of your usage limit; Anthropic suggests starting a new conversation if you're approaching your usage limit in a longer chat. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

About the author (from the house rules): Mojeed Abisiga is a data and AI leader and educator whose mission is to make data and AI easy for everyone; he teaches people to use AI at work. [https://mojeedabisiga.com/]

Memory import: only memory can be imported from another AI provider, not conversation history. Go to Settings > Your Claude and select 'Start import'; the import flow shows a prompt to use in your old service and a box to paste the result; paste it and click 'Add to memory'. Anthropic calls memory import experimental. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12123587-import-and-export-your-memory-from-claude] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Uploading: click the '+' button in the lower left corner of the chat box and select 'Add files or photos', or drag and drop files into the chat. Images can be up to 8000x8000 pixels; PDFs up to 1000 pages. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-upload-files-to-claude]

Settings sections named in Anthropic's help pages: General and Privacy [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]; Your Claude [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]; Capabilities [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]; Usage [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]; Billing [https://claude.com/pricing]; Cowork [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork].

Anthropic's prompting guide: think of Claude as a brilliant but new employee who lacks context on your norms and workflows; the more precisely you explain what you want, the better the result. Key test: show your prompt to a colleague with minimal context on the task and ask them to follow it; if they'd be confused, Claude will be too. If you want Claude to do more than the task strictly requires, ask for it explicitly. Setting a role focuses Claude's behaviour and tone; even a single sentence makes a difference. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices]

Anthropic's article for Claude app users warns against over-engineering: longer, more complex prompts are not always better, the first prompt rarely works perfectly, and you should test and refine. [https://claude.com/resources/articles/best-practices-for-prompt-engineering]

Tell Claude what to do rather than what not to do: Anthropic's example asks for 'smoothly flowing prose paragraphs' instead of 'Do not use markdown'. Match your prompt's style to the output you want: removing markdown from your prompt can reduce markdown in the output. Give the reason behind an instruction: Anthropic's example replaces 'NEVER use ellipses' with an explanation that the response will be read aloud by a text-to-speech engine, because Claude can generalise from the explanation. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices]

Examples: Anthropic calls examples one of the most reliable ways to steer Claude's output format, tone and structure; its developer docs recommend 3 to 5 relevant, diverse examples wrapped in <example> tags. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices] Its article for Claude app users says to start with one example and add more only if the output still doesn't match, and notes that recent models pay very close attention to details in examples. [https://claude.com/resources/articles/best-practices-for-prompt-engineering]

Long documents: with long inputs (20k+ tokens), put the documents near the top of the prompt and the question at the end; Anthropic says queries at the end can improve response quality by up to 30% in tests, especially with complex, multi-document inputs. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices] Ask Claude to extract word-for-word quotes first and base its answer on them, and to back each claim with a supporting quote or retract it; these techniques reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations]

Allow Claude to say 'I don't know': explicitly giving Claude permission to admit uncertainty can drastically reduce false information (Anthropic's guide to reducing hallucinations). [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations]

Web search and web fetch count toward usage limits, and a link to a long article pulls the entire article into Claude's context: Anthropic's example is that summarising a 10,000-word article uses substantially more than a regular web search. Free accounts can use web search, with a warning that fetching long pages uses a lot of usage. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10684626-enable-and-use-web-search] Research started in Claude Mobile only searches the web and skips connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-use-research-on-claude]

On paid plans, project knowledge automatically switches to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) near context limits, expanding capacity by up to 10x. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects]

File creation: code execution and file creation is available to all users on web, desktop and mobile; Claude can generate Excel, PowerPoint, Word and PDF files, and it is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude] Anthropic's built-in skills handle Excel, Word, PowerPoint and PDF creation and are used automatically when relevant. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude]

Artifacts: an artifact is anything Claude makes that you'd put in front of someone (a design, deck, document, dashboard or small interactive tool); it opens beside the conversation and can be edited and shared; artifacts are on all plans. Templates: Docs, Slides and Design on all plans; Data on paid plans; Sheets and Whiteboards in beta on paid plans. Claude Slides can be edited slide by slide, presented inside Claude and exported to PowerPoint or PDF. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them] Claude doesn't make photos or illustrations; it builds diagrams, charts and interactive visuals with HTML and SVG. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9002504-can-claude-produce-images]

Custom skills: package the skill folder as a ZIP, go to Customize > Skills, click '+', then '+ Create skill' and 'Upload a skill'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude] In the sidebar, what was Customize becomes Plugins, and one Plugins page replaces the separate Skills, Connectors and Plugins tabs: available now on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, Team from 30 November 2026, Enterprise in the following weeks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17740565-manage-plugins-skills-and-connectors-from-one-plugins-page]

Models: Anthropic recommends starting most coding and knowledge tasks with Opus 5.5 as the 'strongest daily driver', moving up to Fable or down to Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 as needed. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2] Sonnet 5.5 is positioned as strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks and creating polished documents, slides and spreadsheets; Opus 5.5 for complex work needing careful judgment. In the Claude apps the default effort is Medium. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5] Haiku 5.5 is built for high-volume work. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5] For chat users, Anthropic recommends the most efficient Haiku model or the most recent Sonnet model for most tasks, because they cost fewer tokens than Opus models. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans] On the Free plan the pricing table shows Sonnet and Haiku, not Opus or Fable. [https://claude.com/pricing] To make Claude think less on the newest models, choose a lower effort. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]

Usage credits let Pro, Max and Ultra users keep working after hitting limits at standard API rates; turn them on in Settings > Usage with a monthly spend limit; when work switches to credits, the limit warning changes to 'Now using credits'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-manage-usage-credits-for-paid-claude-plans] Limit resets restore a five-hour, weekly or Fable limit via 'Reset for free' in Settings > Usage; a reset can't be undone, and an unused reset is lost if you downgrade or cancel. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17007452-what-is-a-limit-reset] A length limit (one chat's context window) is different from usage limits; Anthropic's fix for it is to start a new conversation or use projects. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Anthropic's usage tips for Cowork: group related work into one task instead of several; start a new conversation for unrelated work, so Claude isn't carrying extra context; tell Claude when you only need a quick answer, not a file or finished deliverable; check your usage in Settings > Usage. Multi-step tasks use more usage than a quick question. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Connectors inherit each person's permissions from the connected service. Browse and add them from a chat via '+' > 'Connectors' > 'Manage connectors', or from Customize > Connectors. To make Claude ask before each use of a specific connector tool: Customize > Connectors > select the connector > Permissions tab > Tool permissions > 'Always ask' (rolling out gradually). [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Claude Cowork brings Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding: you describe an outcome, step away and come back to finished work such as formatted documents, organised files and synthesised research. It is on paid plans only (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise). To start: in the message box, select 'Cowork', describe the task, review Claude's approach, then let it run. In the new Claude experience there's no 'Cowork' option: you describe the task in any conversation. Tasks run in the cloud, so work continues if you close your laptop; local files, the browser and computer use need Claude Desktop open. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile] Cowork uses more of your limit because it coordinates multiple sub-agents and tool calls. [https://claude.com/product/cowork]

Cowork folders and instructions: Claude can only read and write files in folders you have connected. Anthropic advises creating a dedicated working folder for Claude instead of granting broad access, and keeping backups of important files. Claude must get your permission ('Allow') before permanently deleting files. Global instructions: Settings > Cowork, click 'Edit' next to Global instructions, type them and click 'Save'; in the new Claude experience they became part of Instructions in Settings > Your Claude. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Approval modes, changed at any time from the mode selector in the chat box: 'Manually approve' (Manual, formerly 'Ask before acting'): Claude pauses for Allow/Deny on actions; 'Automatically approve' (Auto): Claude keeps working and an automated check reviews each action, blocking unsafe ones, and if blocked repeatedly it switches back to asking; 'Skip all approvals' (Skip, formerly 'Act without asking'): nothing checks Claude's actions, use only when you completely trust every action, connector, file and app involved. Auto can miss risky actions; for work involving money, messages sent as you or important files, stay close or switch to Manual. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] Auto is rolling out as the default on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team; Manual is the default on Enterprise. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude] Switch to Manually approve when a task touches sensitive files, accounts or sites, uses a new tool, plugin or site, or when mistakes would be hard to undo, like sending messages or making purchases. You remain responsible for all actions Claude takes on your behalf. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Scheduled tasks run a saved prompt on a recurring basis or on demand, on all paid plans, in Cowork and the new Claude experience. Type /schedule in any Cowork task, or click 'Scheduled' in the left sidebar. On the Scheduled tasks page, 'New task' (upper right) offers 'Create with Claude' (Claude asks questions, then you click 'Schedule') or 'Set up manually', which asks for a task name, prompt, approval mode, frequency (hourly, daily, weekly, on weekdays, or manually), an optional model and an optional folder. Picking a folder turns on 'Require this computer', so the task runs only while the computer is awake and Claude Desktop is open; otherwise tasks run remotely even when the computer is asleep. From the Scheduled page you can review upcoming and past runs, edit, pause, resume, delete or run a task on demand. In the new experience, describe the task and how often in any conversation, review Claude's proposal, then click 'Schedule'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] Safety advice: start simple, don't schedule tasks that access sensitive files, send messages on your behalf, make purchases or take hard-to-undo actions, review outputs after each run, and pause tasks you're not using. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Computer use lets Claude operate your screen (clicking, typing, opening apps) when it has no connector or tool for the job; Claude tries connectors first, then the browser, then the screen. Available on Pro, Max and Ultra in Cowork and Claude Code in Claude Desktop for macOS and Windows (beta on Team and Enterprise; not on Linux). Turn it on in the desktop app at Settings > Capabilities (or Settings > System, under This computer): 'Enable computer use'. Claude asks permission before each app; browsers and many trading apps are view-only, terminals and code editors allow click and scroll but no typing, most other apps get full access; some apps are off limits and you can block apps. Computer use is not limited to connected folders and deletion protection does not cover it. Anthropic recommends not granting access to sensitive apps (banking, healthcare, government) and starting with simple tasks. The computer must be awake with Claude Desktop open, and screen interaction is slower than connectors.
